title: decoupled-prefetch-kv-residency-and-priority-fairness-proposal
content:
Context and goal:
This doc explores a design where prefetch (token/profile-level KV fetch + prefix work) is decoupled from token-emit decode execution more explicitly than today. The objective: improve fairness across mixed-latency streams, reduce KV thrashing for long-running chats, and give the kernel selection layer better signals for occupancy so we can avoid pathological slowdowns under load.

Why a new approach?
- We see two recurring issues in production: (1) long chat sessions with frequent short decodes monopolize KV residency and evict hot prefixes for larger single-shot inferences; (2) conflating prefill and decode kernels forces conservative decode batch sizes to avoid KV misses, hurting throughput for high-throughput customers.
- The proposal is not a radical pipeline rewrite; it is a scheduler + KV residency policy + lightweight API surface to let the runtime treat prefetch as a first-class stage with its own resource accounting and fairness knobs.

High-level design overview:
1) Two logical stages with clear resource quotas:
   - Prefetch stage: responsible for reading KV shards, priming KV cache, evaluating cheap prefix-only kernels (e.g., rotary/embedding transforms, attention state setup).
   - Emit (decode) stage: runs autoregressive token generation kernels using already-primed KV state.

   These stages can overlap: prefetch can run for other streams while a different stream is in emit, but each stream must acquire a lightweight token of "KV residency" (a lease) before decode starts.

2) KV residency tiers and soft-residency:
   - Resident: full KV cached on local GPU / node (fastest).
   - Warm: small compressed/quantized KV in LRU holder (restore cost ~10-25ms).
   - Cold: KV must be fetched from remote or rebuild from checkpoints (higher latency).

   Residency is tracked per-stream with a score (float) rather than boolean. Score decays over time and is bumped by prefetch work. Eviction uses an aging-aware policy (see metrics).

3) Priority + fairness policy (soft-priority aging):
   - Each request gets a priority class and a fairness weight. Priority classes: realtime, interactive, batch.
   - Scheduler uses "soft-priority aging": a stream's effective priority increases gradually when it waits for KV residency or emit scheduling for > X ms. This prevents starvation of lower-priority long-running chats.

   EffectivePriority = BasePriority + alpha * waiting_seconds + beta * (1 - KV_residency_score)

4) Microbatch windowing and dynamic kernel hints:
   - Scheduler groups emit-stage tokens into microbatches based on per-model kernel hints (preferred microbatch size for latency/throughput tradeoff). Hints are provided by kernel selector using historical occupancy and sequence-length distribution.
   - When KV_residency_score < threshold, the scheduler reduces microbatch size to avoid wasting work on tokens that will become blocked by KV fetches.

5) Backpressure and prefetch admission control:
   - Prefetch tasks are admission-controlled by a separate quota to avoid overloading memory or PCIe bandwidth.
   - If prefetch capacity is saturated, new prefetch requests are queued in a prioritized FIFO; they can be dropped to cold fetch fallback if latency SLOs require it.

API/flags (runtime config):
- prefetch.enabled: boolean (default true)
- prefetch.max_concurrent_per_node: int (default 64)
- residency.min_warm_score: float (0.2)
- scheduler.soft_age_alpha: float (0.1)
- scheduler.kv_aware_microbatching: boolean

Metrics to emit (for rollout and debugging):
- kv_residency_score_{stream_id} (gauge)
- prefetch_wait_ms (histogram)
- prefetch_failures / prefetch_evictions (counter)
- effective_priority_distribution (histogram)
- microbatch_size_histogram_by_model (histogram)
- tail_latency_95/99 for emit stage with tags for residency tier

Operational behaviors and fallbacks:
- If a stream cannot obtain resident or warm KV before decode deadline, runtime will: (1) optionally start decode on a smaller model-variant (quantized/short-context), or (2) stream a partial response with "progressive fidelity" and mark for re-prefetch for the next token window.
- On memory pressure, reduce prefetch.max_concurrent_per_node and proactively demote warm residents to compressed warm to free space.

Scheduler pseudocode (sketch):
  while true:
    ready_emits = get_ready_emit_streams()  # streams with KV lease and tokens to emit
    if ready_emits not empty:
      ranked = sort_by_effective_priority(ready_emits)
      batch = create_microbatch(ranked, kernel_hints)
      schedule_emit(batch)
    else:
      # do prefetch work if idle slots exist
      pending_prefetch = pick_prefetch_by_priority()
      if pending_prefetch and prefetch_quota_available():
        launch_prefetch(pending_prefetch)
      else:
        sleep(short_interval)
Open questions / risks:
- How to tune alpha/beta for soft-priority aging across very different workloads? Recommend an experiment sweep in staging with A/B across alpha in {0.05, 0.1, 0.25} and beta in {0.2, 0.5}.
- Prefix-only kernel correctness: some model variants do nontrivial per-token state updates in prefill; need to audit model loader to ensure prefetch kernels are functionally identical to in-decode prefix setup.
- Eviction oscillation: frequent demote/promote may thrash PCIe. Consider hysteresis windows and a sample-based eviction policy.

Rollout plan (minimum viable rollout):
- Phase 0: Local sim harness + unit tests for residency scoring and scheduler ranking (2 wks)
- Phase 1: Canary on a small pool (internal customers + low-traffic tenancy) with metrics collectors (4 wks)
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp with automated rollback if tail p99 emit latency increases > 10% or prefetch_failures spike > 3x baseline (4 wks)

Experiment ideas to validate benefits:
- Spike test: replay mixed workload (30% realtime short chats, 50% long chats, 20% single-shot large token counts) and compare p99 latency and total tokens/sec vs baseline.
- KV eviction study: instrument residency transitions to measure reduction in cold fetches.
- Throughput uplift: measure tokens/sec for high-throughput customers when kv_aware_microbatching=true vs false.

Implementation notes and PR plan:
- Kernel selector: add lightweight API to expose preferred microbatch_size_hint per model and per-sequence-length-bucket. (PR: gh/serving-runtime #kernel-hints)
- Residency store: implement score as single float per-stream stored in main scheduler; persisted short-term for resumption. Use atomics to avoid locks in hot path.
- Scheduler: incremental change, start with a token-lease abstraction and separate prefetch worker pool.

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype scheduler sketch + unit tests: Ava Chen (owner), Diego Morales (review) — 2 weeks
- Kernel hint integration + microbatch tests: Priya Nair — 2 weeks
- Staging canary + dashboards: Liam O'Connor — 3 weeks

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally conservative: no forced model-variant switching by default, and no cross-node prefetching for now. Focus on reducing local GPU KV churn and improving fair scheduling.
- Look for correctness gaps in prefix kernel behavior — that's the riskiest functional surface.

Scratchpad / unresolved fragments:
- Should warm -> resident promotion require a minimum emission count? e.g., only promote if stream emitted > 4 tokens in the last 60s — TODO experiment
- Should we give a small prefetch budget for best-effort streams that want lower cost? Could be a per-tenant toggle.

References and related work:
- internal: ENG-1423 (early kv eviction experiments)
- related GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/421 (microbatching refactor)
